claim_text: During the 12-month intervention, the charcoal-burning suicide rate in Tuen Mun fell from 4.3 to 2.0 per 100,000 (a 53.5% reduction), while the control district increased from 3.0 to 4.3 per 100,000.
population: residents of Tuen Mun and Yuen Long, Hong Kong
intervention_or_exposure: restricted retail access to barbecue charcoal
provenance_locator: British Journal of Psychiatry short report, Results, p. 241

claim_text: The all-method suicide rate in Tuen Mun fell from 17.9 to 12.2 per 100,000 (31.8%), compared with a 1.6% reduction in Yuen Long.
population: residents of Tuen Mun and Yuen Long, Hong Kong
intervention_or_exposure: restricted retail access to barbecue charcoal
provenance_locator: British Journal of Psychiatry short report, Results, p. 241

claim_text: The study did not observe a significant increase in suicide by other methods, providing no clear evidence of method substitution during the intervention period.
population: residents of Tuen Mun and Yuen Long, Hong Kong
intervention_or_exposure: restricted retail access to barbecue charcoal
provenance_locator: British Journal of Psychiatry, Summary and Methods

claim_text: After adjustment for secular trends, the New Taipei charcoal-restriction programme was associated with an estimated 30% reduction in charcoal-burning suicide compared with the pre-intervention period.
population: residents of New Taipei City, Taipei City, and Kaohsiung City, Taiwan
intervention_or_exposure: restricted retail access to barbecue charcoal
provenance_locator: PubMed PMID 26305374, Abstract: Methods and Findings

claim_text: The study reported no compensatory increase in non-charcoal-burning suicide in New Taipei City during the intervention period.
population: residents of New Taipei City, Taipei City, and Kaohsiung City, Taiwan
intervention_or_exposure: restricted retail access to barbecue charcoal
provenance_locator: PubMed PMID 26305374, Abstract: Methods and Findings

claim_text: Across the longer follow-up, the controlled interrupted time-series analysis found no clear reduction in charcoal-burning suicide attributable to the New Taipei restriction programme.
population: residents of New Taipei City and two comparison cities, Taiwan
intervention_or_exposure: restricted retail access to barbecue charcoal
provenance_locator: PubMed PMID 33601720, Abstract: Results and Conclusion

claim_text: The authors highlighted incomplete coverage and lack of legislative enforcement as limitations relevant to interpreting long-term programme effectiveness.
population: residents of New Taipei City and two comparison cities, Taiwan
intervention_or_exposure: restricted retail access to barbecue charcoal

claim_text: Charcoal-burning suicide rose markedly in several, but not all, East and Southeast Asian settings, with substantial variation in timing and scale across countries.
population: populations of selected East and Southeast Asian countries
intervention_or_exposure: regional adoption and spread of charcoal-burning suicide
provenance_locator: PubMed PMID 24691071, Abstract: Results and Conclusions

claim_text: Increases in charcoal-burning suicide were associated with increases in overall suicide in some settings but not consistently across all countries and demographic groups.
population: populations of selected East and Southeast Asian countries
